content: Few people have the wisdom to prefer blame that is useful to them over praise that betrays them.
author: François de La Rochefoucauld
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

Across his life and work, François de La Rochefoucauld saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: How can acknowledging your vulnerability help you build deeper self-trust and inner peace?
